review_candidates.title: IT Operations Manager
review_candidates.description: About The Role Position Summary We are seeking an experienced Site IT Manager to lead IT operations for our Taiwan location, supporting local employees, engineering labs, local server rooms, network infrastructure, and end-user technology services. The role will manage a small local IT team while remaining hands-on with technical issues, infrastructure support, and project delivery. The Site IT Manager will serve as the primary IT partner for local business and engineering teams. This individual will understand local requirements, translate them into actionable IT needs, prioritize demand, and coordinate with regional and HQ IT teams to troubleshoot issues and deploy solutions that meet business requirements and global IT standards. The successful candidate will combine people leadership, service delivery discipline, broad IT operations experience, strong networking knowledge, practical systems expertise, and a hands-on mindset. The individual does not need to be the deepest technical expert in every infrastructure domain, but must be able to understand technical concepts, perform practical troubleshooting, communicate effectively with HQ engineering teams, and drive issues and projects to resolution. Key Responsibilities Site IT Leadership and People Management Lead, coach, and develop a small local IT support team, establishing clear responsibilities, priorities, coverage, and escalation paths. Assign and prioritize team workload based on business impact, operational risk, project commitments, and service expectations. Promote strong customer service, accountability, documentation, knowledge sharing, and continuous improvement within the local IT team. Ensure local IT activities follow company security, infrastructure, change management, and operational standards. Serve as the primary local escalation point for significant IT issues and coordinate the appropriate technical resources through resolution. Business Partnership and IT Demand Management Serve as the primary IT point of contact for Taiwan site leadership, business functions, and engineering teams. Build effective relationships with local stakeholders and maintain regular communication regarding IT needs, issues, priorities, risks, and upcoming changes. Understand business and engineering requirements and translate them into clear technical requirements, support needs, or project requests. Collect, document, evaluate, and prioritize local IT demand, including new capabilities, infrastructure changes, equipment, access, and service requests. Coordinate with HQ and regional IT teams to review requirements, identify solutions, obtain required approvals, and execute agreed implementations. Communicate realistic expectations, dependencies, risks, status, and resolution plans to both technical and non-technical stakeholders. IT Operations and Service Delivery Own day-to-day local IT operations and ensure reliable delivery of end-user, infrastructure, network, and site technology services. Coordinate incident, service request, problem, escalation, and change management activities for the site. Monitor recurring issues, service performance, capacity, and operational risks, and drive corrective or preventive improvements. Maintain accurate operational documentation, support procedures, infrastructure diagrams, configuration information, and troubleshooting knowledge. Coordinate onboarding, offboarding, workstation provisioning, access, and other local IT lifecycle activities with appropriate enterprise teams. Work with vendors, contractors, and service providers and ensure local work is completed safely, professionally, and according to requirements. IT Asset, Inventory, and Lifecycle Management Maintain accurate inventory and ownership records for local IT hardware, infrastructure equipment, peripherals, and other managed technology assets. Coordinate equipment demand, procurement support, receiving, deployment, refresh, warranty, spare inventory, reuse, and secure disposal activities. Plan site technology needs proactively based on hiring, projects, engineering requirements, lifecycle status, capacity, and business demand. Ensure asset records and physical inventory remain aligned with company asset management and security requirements. Network and Infrastructure Support Support and troubleshoot wired and wireless LAN, WAN connectivity, network services, and site infrastructure. Provide hands-on support for switches, network connectivity, server-room infrastructure, rack equipment, cabling, and related hardware when required. Understand enterprise networking concepts including TCP/IP, DNS, DHCP, VLANs, routing, switching, wireless, and Layer 2/Layer 3 troubleshooting. Coordinate complex network incidents, design questions, configuration changes, and deployments with HQ network engineering teams. Maintain site network diagrams, rack information, cabling records, infrastructure documentation, and operational procedures. Monitor local infrastructure health and identify capacity, reliability, supportability, or lifecycle concerns before they impact the business. Systems and Infrastructure Coordination Provide practical support and troubleshooting for Windows clients, Windows Server environments, Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, DNS, DHCP, Group Policy, virtualization, storage, backup, and related infrastructure services. Perform appropriate first-level or hands-on troubleshooting, gather technical evidence, and engage HQ systems engineers for advanced diagnosis, architecture, or configuration changes. Coordinate server, virtual machine, storage, backup, identity, and infrastructure requests with enterprise engineering teams. Support server-room equipment deployment, rack and stack activities, structured cabling, and physical connectivity when required. Engineering Lab Support Partner with local engineering teams to understand lab computing, network, connectivity, infrastructure, and equipment requirements. Support lab-related IT incidents and deployments and coordinate specialized requirements with HQ engineering and infrastructure teams. Help ensure lab technology changes follow appropriate security, network, documentation, and change-control requirements. Provide hands-on troubleshooting in the engineering lab when appropriate and coordinate escalation for complex technical issues. Project and Change Delivery Lead or support local IT projects involving infrastructure, office technology, engineering lab support, end-user services, network changes, and business technology deployment. Coordinate requirements, technical resources, implementation plans, testing, change requests, stakeholder communication, risk management, and operational handoff. Work closely with HQ IT project managers, architects, engineers, security teams, and service owners to deliver solutions successfully. Remain hands-on during implementation and troubleshooting when local physical or technical support is required. Ensure completed projects include appropriate documentation, support ownership, and transition into normal operations. End-User Technology Support Ensure effective support for Windows endpoints, Microsoft 365 services, applications, printers, peripherals, conference-room technology, and remote support needs. Provide direct hands-on support for priority, complex, or escalated user issues when needed. Coordinate workstation deployment, imaging, software installation, licensing, access, SSO, and MFA issues with the appropriate enterprise teams. Promote a strong customer-service culture and ensure users receive clear communication throughout the support process. Required Qualifications Bachelor's degree in Information Technology, Computer Science, Engineering, or a related field, or equivalent practical experience. Approximately 7+ years of progressive enterprise IT experience, including broad exposure to infrastructure, networking, end-user services, and IT operations. Experience leading a local IT function, technical team, or site support operation, including work prioritization and team coordination. Strong networking knowledge and practical troubleshooting experience across LAN, WAN, wireless, VLANs, routing, switching, DNS, and DHCP. Broad working knowledge of Windows Server, Active Directory, Microsoft Entra ID, virtualization, storage, backup, and enterprise infrastructure concepts. Experience with IT service delivery processes such as incident, request, problem, change, escalation, and service-level management. Experience managing IT assets, inventory, equipment lifecycle, and technology demand. Experience coordinating or delivering infrastructure and technology projects. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to work effectively with business users, engineering teams, leadership, vendors, and remote HQ technical teams. Strong analytical and troubleshooting skills with a practical, hands-on mindset. Ability to work independently, manage multiple priorities, make sound operational decisions, and escalate appropriately. Preferred Qualifications And Technical Experience Experience supporting engineering, R&D, manufacturing, lab, or other technically complex site environments. Cisco enterprise networking experience; familiarity with technologies such as STP, HSRP, OSPF, BGP, EIGRP, Cisco ISE, RADIUS, TACACS+, or NAC is beneficial. Experience with VMware/ESXi, virtual networking, enterprise storage, monitoring, backup, and recovery technologies. Linux administration and SSH-based troubleshooting experience. PowerShell, Ansible, scripting, or infrastructure automation experience. Experience with ITIL-aligned service management and Jira or comparable ticket/service management platforms. Hands-on experience with rack and stack activities, structured copper and fiber cabling, server-room operations, video conferencing, and workstation deployment. Core Competencies People leadership and team development Business partnership and stakeholder communication Customer-focused service delivery Infrastructure and network troubleshooting Hands-on technical ownership Demand prioritization and operational planning Project and change coordination Root-cause analysis and problem solving Cross-functional collaboration with local and HQ teams Documentation, organization, and continuous improvement Success in This Role Success in this position means the Taiwan site has a dependable local IT leader who understands the business, keeps day-to-day IT operations under control, develops the local support team, maintains strong infrastructure and network support, manages technology demand and assets effectively, and works seamlessly with HQ IT teams. The manager should be equally comfortable discussing requirements with local leaders, troubleshooting an issue in the lab or server room, and coordinating a complex solution with remote engineering specialists. review_candidates.title: Senior Systems Engineer
review_candidates.description: Job Description The Senior Systems Engineer is responsible for the administration, performance, security, and continued improvement of the organization’s enterprise infrastructure. This position manages complex server, storage, backup, virtualization, email, and cloud environments while identifying opportunities to improve efficiency through automation and system optimization. The Senior Systems Engineer also serves as a technical leader, supporting IT staff, implementing best practices, and helping align infrastructure solutions with evolving business needs. Responsibilities Administer, monitor, maintain, and optimize on-premises and cloud-based infrastructure. Manage enterprise server, storage, virtualization, backup, and email environments. Support cloud services with a focus on security, scalability, performance, and cost efficiency. Monitor system health and performance, troubleshoot complex technical issues, and conduct capacity planning. Develop automation solutions using scripting and DevOps tools to streamline system processes and deployments. Lead disaster recovery and business continuity efforts to ensure system availability and data protection. Implement cybersecurity best practices, security hardening, monitoring, and risk mitigation strategies. Research, evaluate, and deploy new technologies that support organizational and business needs. Provide technical leadership and mentorship to IT staff and promote infrastructure best practices. Maintain accurate technical documentation, system configurations, procedures, and policies. Collaborate with cross-functional teams to design and implement effective technology solutions. Provide advanced technical support for software, hardware, and infrastructure-related issues. Travel as needed, work varied shifts including weekends and holidays, and perform other job-related duties as assigned. Qualifications Bachelor’s degree in Computer Science, Information Systems, or a related field and 5+ years of experience in systems engineering or IT infrastructure management; equivalent combinations of education and experience may be considered. Advanced experience with Windows Server, Linux, enterprise storage, backup solutions, and email platforms such as Exchange and Microsoft 365. Strong knowledge of cloud platforms such as Microsoft Azure, AWS, or Google Cloud and hybrid-cloud infrastructure strategies. Experience with enterprise backup technologies such as Veeam, Commvault, Rubrik, or similar solutions. Experience with virtualization technologies including VMware and Hyper-V. Advanced scripting and automation skills using PowerShell, Python, Bash, or similar technologies. Strong knowledge of cybersecurity, system hardening, endpoint security, data protection, and email security protocols including DKIM, SPF, and DMARC. Experience with performance monitoring, capacity planning, disaster recovery, and system automation tools. Certifications such as Microsoft Certified: Azure Solutions Architect, AWS Certified SysOps Administrator, VMware Certified Professional (VCP), or ITIL are preferred. Strong analytical, troubleshooting, organizational, and problem-solving skills with the ability to manage multiple priorities in a fast-paced environment. Excellent communication and collaboration skills with the ability to provide technical leadership and work effectively across teams. Ability to lift up to 50 pounds, work in varying environments, travel as required, and work varied schedules. Ability to obtain and maintain required gaming licensure and a valid driver’s license. review_candidates.title: Network Engineer II
review_candidates.description: Your Role at Tessy The Network Engineer is responsible for the design, implementation, security, reliability and day-to-day operation of Tessy Plastics' enterprise network infrastructure across corporate, manufacturing and remote environments. This position will provide senior-level technical leadership for Tessy's routing, switching, wireless, firewalls, SD-WAN, network access control, VPN, voice and collaboration and related network technologies. The Network Engineer will ensure the network is secure, highly available, scalable and capable of supporting the company's business and manufacturing operations. The role will work closely with Information Services, Cybersecurity, Infrastructure, Automation, Engineering and business teams to design and maintain secure connectivity between traditional IT environments, manufacturing/OT systems, cloud services and remote locations. The Network Engineer will also lead or participate in network projects, technology upgrades, troubleshooting, incident response, infrastructure improvements and the development of network standards and documentation. Occasional after-hours and weekend work may be required for planned maintenance, upgrades and critical incidents. What You'll Be Doing Design, implement, configure, maintain and troubleshoot enterprise LAN, WAN, wireless and network security infrastructure. Manage and support enterprise routing, switching, VLANs, subnetting, NAT, ACLs, routing protocols and network segmentation. Administer and maintain enterprise firewalls, VPN technologies, network security policies and secure remote connectivity. Monitor network availability, performance, capacity and security and proactively identify and resolve potential issues before they impact the business. Design and maintain highly available and redundant network solutions to maximize uptime and business continuity. Manage and support enterprise wireless infrastructure, including wireless controllers, access points, authentication, coverage and performance. Support and maintain SD-WAN and multi-site network connectivity, including coordination with telecommunications and Internet service providers. Support data center networking and related technologies, including core switching, network fabrics and high-speed connectivity. Support network access control and authentication technologies used to secure corporate and manufacturing environments. Work closely with Automation and Engineering teams to securely connect manufacturing and industrial systems to the enterprise network while maintaining appropriate IT/OT segmentation and security controls. Administer and support network-related voice and collaboration technologies, including VoIP, voice gateways, unified communications, conference room systems and related services. Support network services including DHCP, DNS, IP address management, network authentication and related infrastructure. Participate in cybersecurity initiatives involving network security, vulnerability remediation, firewall security, network segmentation, access control and incident response. Lead or participate in network upgrades, migrations, technology implementations, infrastructure refreshes and other network-related projects. Perform root-cause analysis for complex or recurring network issues and implement permanent corrective actions. Develop and maintain network standards, architecture documentation, network diagrams, configurations, operating procedures and troubleshooting runbooks. Maintain accurate records of network devices, IP addressing, VLANs, circuits, configurations and related infrastructure. Identify opportunities to automate network administration, monitoring, reporting, configuration and provisioning activities. Participate in change management, incident management, problem management and other IT service management processes. Work with vendors and service providers to troubleshoot issues, manage support cases, evaluate solutions and coordinate installations and upgrades. Assist with network disaster recovery and business continuity planning and participate in recovery testing. Provide technical leadership, mentoring and knowledge transfer to other members of the Information Services team. Provide senior-level escalation support for complex network incidents and problems. Maintain appropriate documentation for tickets, changes, projects and operational activities. Participate in an on-call rotation and perform scheduled maintenance outside of normal business hours when required. What You'll Bring Bachelor's degree in Computer Science, Information Technology, Engineering, or a related field preferred; equivalent combination of education and experience will be considered. Cisco CCNA, CCNP, Palo Alto, or other relevant industry certifications are preferred but not required. Demonstrated experience and technical proficiency may be considered in lieu of specific certifications or formal education. 7+ years or equivalent demonstrated experience in enterprise network engineering, administration, troubleshooting and design. Strong hands-on experience with enterprise routing and switching technologies. Demonstrated experience designing, implementing and supporting LAN, WAN and wireless networks. Strong understanding of TCP/IP, VLANs, subnetting, routing, switching, NAT, DHCP, DNS, VPN and network security concepts. Experience administering enterprise firewalls and implementing firewall policies and security controls. Experience troubleshooting complex network issues using packet analysis, logs, monitoring tools and other diagnostic techniques. Experience supporting highly available and redundant network environments. Experience with network monitoring, performance management and capacity planning. Strong understanding of network security, segmentation, access control and secure remote connectivity. Ability to analyze complex technical problems, identify root cause and develop effective solutions. Strong written and verbal communication skills with the ability to communicate technical information to both technical and non-technical audiences. Ability to work independently, prioritize multiple projects and incidents and make sound technical decisions. Strong documentation and organizational skills. Ability to participate in scheduled after-hours maintenance and an on-call rotation. Preferred: Cisco Catalyst switching and enterprise routing Cisco Nexus switching and data center networking VXLAN and network fabric technologies Palo Alto firewalls Cisco DNA Center Cisco Wireless LAN Controllers and enterprise wireless VeloCloud/VMware SD-WAN Forescout or other Network Access Control (NAC) technologies Cisco Umbrella or other DNS security platforms IPAM solutions Cisco CUCM, voice gateways, VoIP and unified communications Cisco Webex and collaboration technologies Microsoft NPS and network authentication Network automation and scripting, including PowerShell, Python, Ansible, or similar technologies Cloud networking, including Azure and/or AWS Manufacturing, industrial, or OT networking environments IT/OT network segmentation and secure integration of industrial systems Additional Expectations Demonstrates a commitment to continuous improvement and staying current with emerging networking and cybersecurity technologies. Works collaboratively with Information Services, Cybersecurity, Automation, Engineering and business teams. Maintains a strong focus on security, reliability, availability and customer service. Willingness to share knowledge, mentor team members and contribute to the development of network standards and best practices. Compensation Salary Range: $115,000–$130,000.
